text: Consistency check: the five turnaround views and the close-ups agree on proportions, the soft gold coat with ivory face, chest and belly, the darker golden ear tips, spine stripe and foot tips, the amber glossy eyes, the brown nose and pads, the crystal spiral horn rising from a crown tuft, the cream-gold inner ears and the cotton-puff tail. Every must-have from the description is present: small bunny body, golden fur, a single horn atop the head, very long lop ears, very large eyes, large springing hind legs (clearest in the side and three-quarter views). Contradictions listed for the blockout to settle: (1) the top view is drawn from above and behind at an angle rather than straight down; (2) the bare-body front barely differs from the furred front, so fur depth should be read from the bare side and back views; (3) the ears hang slightly shorter in the bare side view than in the furred views, where they reach near the ground; (4) the horn's height above the ears varies a little between views. The glow is left out of the sheet on purpose; it belongs to the surface stage. The first turnaround attempt (small hind legs, too saturated a gold, faint tips) was set aside; the sheet was redrawn once.
